answers.explanation: 64 is the starting TTL for macOS, iOS, Linux, and Android. Nothing has decremented it, so it's zero hops away. (172.20.10.x is the range an iPhone hotspot uses.)
Pinging your own address never leaves the machine either, so it's about as fast as loopback. The phone at 172.20.10.1 took about 3 ms over WiFi.
Many routers start TTL at 255. A full 255 means zero hops away.
On a busy WiFi link, short bursts of loss like this are common. The replies before and after show the host is still there.
Steady times mean a quiet link. Wild jumps and a few losses point to congestion or interference.
56 bytes of data plus an 8-byte ICMP header: 64.
min/avg/max: the middle number is the average.
